research: Lines: slate Boston -8.5, which is also the archive close; the archive open is -9.5, so the line came 1 point toward Orlando. The slate equals the close, so there is no slate value either way (slate archive). Spread-specific, neutral.

[angle] Boston is on the second night of a back-to-back after beating Dallas Sunday, when it led 42-9 after the first quarter, the biggest opening-quarter lead in franchise history; Tatum played 30 minutes (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Fatigue and a possible letdown help Orlando +8.5.

Paolo Banchero (ankle) is out again after playing only 2 games this season, and Jonathan Isaac, Noah Penda and Izaiyah Nelson are out too (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). This is a long-standing absence that is already priced. Helps Boston slightly.
Boston is 11-2 and has won 6 straight and 11 of 12. Its +11.6 net rating is 2nd in the NBA (119.2 ORtg, 107.6 DRtg, Basketball Reference via Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Boston -8.5.

Orlando is 5-7 with a 109.7 offensive rating (26th) but has won 3 straight (Sacramento, Utah, Milwaukee). Franz Wagner had 35 points, 12 assists and 9 rebounds vs Milwaukee (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Mixed: weak offense, but improving form.

Spread-specific: the Simple Rating System gap is almost 12 points before home court; after the back-to-back and schedule adjustments the Predictem author still puts it north of 8.5 and projects 113-100 (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Boston, but a preview model is already priced.

[angle] Turnover matchup: Orlando turns it over on 14.9% of possessions (5th-worst), Boston forces turnovers at a top-5 rate, and Boston turned Orlando's 18 turnovers into 21 points in its 108-97 win on Nov 1 (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Boston.

[angle] Three-point variance: Boston shot 12-for-44 from three in the Nov 1 meeting and still won by 11. Boston leads the NBA in threes made but is 29th in threes allowed, and Orlando generates the most wide-open threes per NBA.com (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Desmond Bane has 4+ threes in 7 of 11 games. This cuts both ways: high variance, which helps the underdog's backdoor chances.

Boston plays the slowest pace in the NBA and takes nearly half its shots from three (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). A slow pace limits blowout potential, which helps Orlando +8.5 modestly. The lessons say pace isn't a reason on its own.
Orlando ranks 4th in defensive rebounding percentage, which limits Boston's second chances (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Orlando.
Payton Pritchard hurt his shoulder before the Nov 1 meeting and went 0-for-7 from three in it. He shoots 41.9% from three at home vs 32.7% on the road (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Boston at home.
History: Orlando has lost 23 of its last 28 games in Boston (Magic game notes via Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Venue history is priced, so this is a tiebreaker at most for Boston.
Totals context: the total moved from 211.5 to 212.5 (slate archive), and Covers leans Over 212.5 (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Neutral for the side.
games.reasoning: I project Boston by about 9 against a slate and close of -8.5, which is inside the pass band. Boston's back-to-back after a historic blowout is the main angle for Orlando; Orlando's turnover problem without Banchero is the main case for Boston. A clear status change (for example Tatum sitting the second night of the back-to-back) would have tipped it to Orlando.

research: Lines: slate Cleveland -9.5; the archive open is -10.5 and the close -8.5, so the line moved 2 points toward Chicago. Predictem says the line opened -10.5 and moved down a point, and Covers lists -9.5 (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Spread-specific: the market drifted to Chicago, and the slate is 1 point worse for a Bulls backer than the close.
Spread-specific: Cleveland is 5-9 ATS overall and 3-4 ATS at home; Chicago is 7-5 ATS (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Chicago, but ATS records are priced.

Evan Mobley (16.9 ppg) misses his third straight game with a sprained big toe; coach Kenny Atkinson said he 'looks better already' (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Already known, so priced. Helps Chicago slightly.

[angle] Cleveland sat its usual starters Saturday after travel problems in South Florida and still beat Dallas 127-117 behind Tyrese Proctor's first career triple-double (24 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists). Mitchell, Harden and Allen are now off the injury report (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Rested starters return, which helps Cleveland.
Harden's calf is flagged as a concern, and Peyton Watson and Jaylon Tyson are questionable for Cleveland (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Chicago if Harden is limited.
Caleb Wilson (18.9 ppg, second on the Bulls) is out with a fractured hand; Tobe Awaka is out and Jalen Smith (finger) is questionable (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Cleveland.

[angle] Chicago has won 2 straight without Wilson, including at Minnesota Saturday with 54 paint points, ending the Wolves' 5-game win streak. Norman Powell has taken 19 shots in each game without Wilson and has a 32.1% usage rate (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Chicago: the offense still functions.

Chicago's defense ranks 29th in defensive rating and allows 125.9 ppg and a league-high 31.3 two-point field goals per game. The Bulls are 28th in turnovers (17.3 per game) and play at the NBA's fastest pace (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Cleveland, whose offense ranks 7th in rating.

Spread-specific: a fast pace and a 241.5 total (archive open and close) mean many possessions. That can widen the margin, but it also leaves room for a backdoor cover at a double-digit spread, a risk Predictem flags (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral.
Cleveland ranks 25th in threes allowed, and Chicago shoots only 31% from three (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Mixed.
Both teams played Friday and Saturday and had Sunday off, so neither has a rest edge (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral.
Cleveland has won 6 of the last 8 meetings (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Head-to-head history is priced, so this is not a reason.
Both previews pick Cleveland -9.5 (Covers projects nothing specific; Predictem projects 125-113) (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Writers' picks are priced, so this is a tiebreaker at most.
games.reasoning: I project Cleveland by about 9, between the slate (-9.5) and the close (-8.5), so it's a pass. Cleveland's rested starters returning against the 29th-ranked defense offsets Mobley's absence, Harden's calf and Cleveland's 5-9 ATS record. The surprising angle was Chicago's competent offense without Wilson, which is why I lean Bulls. Confirmation that Harden was limited would have firmed that lean.

research: Lines: slate Washington +3.5, which is also the archive close; the archive open is +6.5, a 3-point move toward Washington. Predictem says the line opened Memphis -6.5, drifted to -4.5 and some books had -3.5; Covers listed -4.5 (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Spread-specific: the line move is information, likely Memphis frontcourt injury news.

Memphis's frontcourt is questionable: Zach Edey (ankle) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) are day-to-day, Quinten Post is in the concussion protocol, and GG Jackson and Scotty Pippen Jr. are out (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Washington, and it likely explains the line move.
Ty Jerome (25.4 ppg, Memphis's leading scorer) is out with right hip soreness (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Washington, though Memphis beat Brooklyn 129-110 without him Saturday.
Spread-specific: Memphis is 6-0 straight up and 6-0 ATS on the road, with a +8.6 point differential vs Washington's -7.2 (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Memphis, but ATS records are priced.

[angle] Washington is on the second night of a back-to-back after a 147-119 home loss to Houston on Sunday, when Trae Young scored 0 points for the first time in his career and Houston outrebounded Washington 56-35 with 64 paint points. Memphis has been rested since Saturday (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Memphis.
Washington has lost 7 straight by an average of 16.7 points, and its last 10 opponents averaged 119.4 points (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Memphis.

[angle] Rebounding mismatch: Memphis ranks 7th in offensive rebounding percentage (29.7%), Washington 27th in defensive rebounding (68.9%), and Memphis scored 62 paint points vs Brooklyn (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Memphis, but it weakens if Edey and Stewart both sit.

[angle] Bounce-back risk: Young after his first career scoreless game, and Anthony Davis (about 25 points and 10 rebounds) against a thin Memphis frontcourt that could hand him extra boards and free throws (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Washington.
Tre Johnson is out with a back injury, thinning Washington's guard depth; Kyshawn George averages 17.6 ppg over his last 10 games (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Mixed.
Memphis averages 120.6 ppg and allows 111.7; Washington averages 110.6 and allows the 7th-most points (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Memphis.
Both previews pick Memphis -4.5 (Predictem projects 119-110), but they were written at -4.5, and the line closed at -3.5 (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Priced.
games.reasoning: I project Memphis by about 4.5 against Washington +3.5, a 1-point edge: a pass. Washington's back-to-back after a 28-point loss supports Memphis, but the 3-point move toward Washington probably reflects Edey and Stewart's day-to-day status, and per the lessons that move is information, not an overreaction. Confirmation that Edey was playing would have moved me toward a Memphis lean.

research: Lines: slate Brooklyn +5.5; the archive open and close are both +5.5, so there was no move. Predictem says most books are at 5.5 with a few at 6.5 (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Spread-specific: a stable market.
Spread-specific: Philadelphia is 7-7 ATS this season despite an 11-3 record (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). The record says Philadelphia hasn't covered often, but ATS records are priced.

[angle] Philadelphia is on the second night of a back-to-back after a 1 PM Sunday home win over Indiana, 131-124; Brooklyn has been rested since Saturday (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). The afternoon tip softens the fatigue. Helps Brooklyn modestly.

Joel Embiid is day-to-day after sitting Sunday for right-foot injury management, and his status was unresolved in the morning preview (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). A late status like this is a pass trigger.

[angle] Michael Porter Jr. (21.5 ppg, Brooklyn's leading scorer) is expected back after missing the Memphis loss for personal reasons; Jordi Fernandez declined to elaborate (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Brooklyn.
Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow are both out with back issues (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). This thins the frontcourt depth. Mixed or neutral.
Philadelphia is 11-3, 2nd in the East; Tyrese Maxey averages 26.7 ppg and Jaylen Brown scored 31 vs Indiana (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Philadelphia.

Brooklyn is 3-9 and has been outscored most nights, but scored 145 at New Orleans last week. It lost to Memphis 129-110 Saturday, when Memphis had 62 paint points (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Philadelphia.
Philadelphia allows 110.4 ppg (about 108 per 100 possessions); Brooklyn's offense is about 107 per 100 by the author's estimate (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). This points to a modest Philadelphia edge.
Spread-specific: the Predictem author calls the spread 'close to fair', projects Philadelphia 113-107 (a 6-point margin vs a 5.5 line) and plays Under 225.5 instead (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral.
Totals trends: Philadelphia has gone over only twice in 6 road games, and the Nets' road overs are 5 of 8 (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Not relevant to the side.
games.reasoning: I project Philadelphia by about 6 against 5.5, essentially the number, and Embiid's day-to-day status is the kind of late status that decides it, so it's a pass. The back-to-back after an afternoon game and Porter's return both point to Brooklyn, but Philadelphia's defense against Brooklyn's weak offense balances them. Knowing Embiid was out would have tilted me to Brooklyn.

research: Lines: slate Miami +2.5; the archive open is +2.5 and the close +1.5, so the line moved a point toward Miami. The total rose from 228.5 to 233.5 (slate archive). Spread-specific: the market leaned Miami late.

[angle] Houston is on the second night of a back-to-back, flying in from Washington after a 147-119 win Sunday in which Kevin Durant played 30 minutes and Amen Thompson scored 26. Miami is rested at home (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Miami.

Houston's absences: Covers lists Clint Capela and Steven Adams out (a thin frontcourt behind Sengun), Marcus Smart suspended and Amen Thompson questionable. Predictem lists Fred VanVleet (knee) and Capela out and Smart suspended (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). The sources conflict, and Thompson's status is unresolved. Helps Miami.

Spread-specific: by ratings, Houston is +11.25 on the Simple Rating System vs Miami's -1.43; Houston has a 120.3 offensive rating (5th), 111.2 defensive rating (8th) and +9.1 net rating (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Covers lists the net ratings as Houston 13.7 (4th) and Miami 10.9 (6th), another conflict. Helps Houston.
Miami is 7-6 after an 0-4 start, has won 4 straight and 7 of 9, and won its last 3 home games by an average of 17.3, including over Cleveland and Detroit by 12+ (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Miami.
Spread-specific: Miami has covered 6 straight against Houston (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Head-to-head history is priced, so this is a tiebreaker at most.

[angle] Free-throw matchup: Miami has averaged an NBA-high 34.8 FTA per game during its win streak (Giannis and Bam combining for 18.5), and Houston has allowed the 7th-most FTA over its last 4 games (27.8). Without Capela and Adams, Houston has fewer bodies to foul (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Miami.

[angle] Rebounding: Houston's 31.5% offensive rebounding is 2nd in the NBA vs Miami's 23.8% (near the bottom), and Houston outrebounded Washington 55-36 Sunday, but its center absences cut into that edge (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Houston if Sengun carries it.
Miami's defense allows 116.5 per 100 (22nd) and opponents post a .570 eFG%; all 4 streak opponents scored 108+ (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Houston.
Giannis averages 28.9 points and 12.5 rebounds and has cleared 44.5 PRA in 4 straight games; Davion Mitchell leads the NBA at 9.2 assists (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Miami.
The previews split: Covers takes the Heat moneyline, Predictem takes Rockets -2.5 and projects 119-112 (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral and priced.
games.reasoning: I project Houston by about 3 against +2.5 (close 1.5): no edge. Houston's big ratings edge is offset by the back-to-back with travel, a depleted frontcourt and Amen Thompson's questionable tag, and the late move to Miami suggests the market priced those. Thompson's late status is a pass trigger on its own; knowing he played would have firmed a small Houston lean.

research: Lines: slate Minnesota -2.5, with no open or close in the archive. Predictem says the line opened -3.5 and moved to -2.5, with the market leaning Portland (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Spread-specific: a 1-point move toward Portland.
Spread-specific: Minnesota is 11-2 ATS, including 6-0 ATS on the road; Portland is 5-2 ATS on the road (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Both teams have been covering, and these records are priced.

Anthony Edwards is out after knee surgery; Minnesota was 3-1 with him and is 6-3 since. Ayo Dosunmu has averaged 22 points since the injury (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). A long-known absence, so priced.

[angle] Minnesota lost at home to Chicago (3 wins) on Saturday, missing its first 13 threes and scoring a season-low 17 first-quarter points, which ended a 5-game win streak. It has shot only 18-for-71 (.254) from three in its 2 losses vs .385 during the streak (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral: a variance game.

[angle] Portland has the NBA's No. 1 three-point defense (holding 4 of its last 6 opponents under .310) against a Minnesota team whose results swing with its three-point shooting (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Portland.

Portland is 9-3 and 6-1 on the road, swept Oklahoma City in a back-to-back, then won at Sacramento Friday; Deni Avdija averages 23.9 points and 6.2 assists (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Portland.
Portland is without Ja Morant (hamstring) and Shaedon Sharpe (knee) (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Minnesota, though both were out during Portland's run.

[angle] Turnover matchup: Portland commits 16.3 turnovers a game, and Minnesota forces 9.0 steals a game with the top-rated defense (106.8 ppg allowed); LaMelo Ball is 7th in steals (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Minnesota.

Rest: Predictem says Portland has had two days off since Friday, while Minnesota played Saturday (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Covers raises a possible Lillard back-to-back concern, which conflicts (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Unclear, possibly favoring Portland.

Half splits: Portland has the 3rd-highest first-half scoring average; Minnesota has the 2nd-highest second-half average and the league's best second-half margin (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Neutral for the full game.
The teams meet again Tuesday in Minneapolis, so it's a two-game set (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral.
The previews split: Covers takes Portland's moneyline; Predictem takes Minnesota -2.5, projecting 116-111 and calling the edge thin (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral and priced.
games.reasoning: I project Minnesota by about 3 against -2.5, within the pass band. Minnesota's defense against Portland's turnovers is matched by Portland's elite three-point defense against a Wolves team that lives and dies from three, and the 1-point move to Portland goes against Minnesota. With no archive close to check against, there's no reason to go beyond a pass.

research: Lines: slate New Orleans +3.5, which is also the archive close; the archive open is +2.5, so the line moved a point toward Golden State. The total fell from 226.5 to 223.5 (slate archive; Predictem says the spread was up from 2.5). Spread-specific: a small move toward the Warriors.

Golden State is without Stephen Curry (torn right oblique), Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porzingis; Gui Santos is questionable (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps New Orleans, but the absences are known and priced.

[angle] Since Curry's injury, Golden State lost to Houston and was routed 123-85 in San Antonio, where its starters fell into an 18-0 hole. It is 2-4 on the road (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps New Orleans: the Warriors' current form without Curry is poor.
New Orleans is without Trey Murphy III (knee, 5th straight game), Dejounte Murray, Bennedict Mathurin, Trendon Watford and Bryce McGowens (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Golden State.

New Orleans is 4-10, has lost 6 straight and is 3-6 at home; its last 3 home losses (to Brooklyn, Memphis and Denver) came by a combined 73 points (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Golden State.

Spread-specific: the Pelicans' defense is among the league's worst. They allow a league-worst 29.3 assists a game, about 118 per 100 possessions, and opponents have averaged 126.1 points over their last 10, with recent opponents scoring 142, 145, 138 and 139 (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Golden State.

[angle] Revenge spot: Golden State beat New Orleans 138-87 a week earlier in San Francisco (a 51-point margin). Yaxel Lendeborg scored 23 and Brandin Podziemski 25 in that game (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). A rematch after a blowout invites regression and a Pelicans effort bump. Helps New Orleans slightly.

[angle] Zion Williamson averages 21.9 points on 60.2% shooting and has topped 23 in 5 of his last 6; Golden State allows 47 paint points per game (17th), and Draymond Green draws the Zion assignment. New Orleans leads the West in paint scoring (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps New Orleans.
Golden State had won 8 of its last 10 before the current skid and has won 7 of the last 8 meetings with New Orleans (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Head-to-head history is priced.
Rest: the Covers trend says the Warriors are on two days' rest (Over 10-1 in their last 11 such games); the Pelicans' rest is not stated (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Neutral to slightly Golden State.
Both previews pick Warriors -3.5 (Predictem projects 118-110) (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Writers' picks are priced.
games.reasoning: I project Golden State by about 4 against -3.5, essentially on the number, so it's a pass. Two depleted teams: the Warriors look bad without Curry (a 38-point loss at San Antonio), while the Pelicans' defense and their 6-game skid are worse still. The 51-point blowout a week ago is a narrative trap both ways; this season's defensive data slightly favors Golden State.

research: Lines: slate Denver -10.5; the archive open is -10.5 and the close -9.5, so the line moved a point toward Phoenix. Covers lists -9.5 and Predictem -10.5 (slate archive; Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Spread-specific: the slate is a point better than the close for a Suns backer, but the lessons say that alone is not an edge.

[angle] Phoenix is on the second night of a back-to-back after Sunday's afternoon 131-123 loss to the Lakers and now plays at altitude in Denver (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Denver, though the afternoon tip gives Phoenix a little extra recovery.

[angle] In Sunday's game Devin Booker shot 4-for-14 for 17 points (0-for-4 from three) and sat the entire fourth quarter, while Collin Gillespie scored 12 of his 26 in the fourth to cut a 31-point deficit to 5 (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Booker's lighter minutes help Phoenix's legs, and the bench showed fight. Helps Phoenix slightly.
Phoenix is without Mark Williams (shoulder), and Drew Timme (hand) is day-to-day (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Denver.

Spread-specific: Denver's net rating is only +1.9 (117.5 ORtg, 9th; 115.6 DRtg, 19th); on the Simple Rating System, Denver is +2.92 and Phoenix +0.26, and Phoenix has faced the 2nd-toughest schedule. The Predictem author's fair line is about Denver -7 and he projects 117-110 (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). This supports Phoenix +10.5 on the numbers, but ratings are priced.

Rebounding mismatch: Phoenix is the NBA's worst defensive rebounding team (66.6%; opponents grab 33.1% of offensive boards) and allows 57.3 rebounds per game (28th), facing Jokic, who has 13+ rebounds twice in his last 4 games (Predictem; Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Denver.
Phoenix ranks 26th in defensive rating (117.4) and 23rd in opponent eFG% (55.1%), and Denver ranks 2nd in FG% (48.7%) (Covers, Nov 16 2026). Helps Denver.
Phoenix is 5-7, hasn't won a road game and has lost 3 straight on the road; Denver is 7-4 and has won 4 of 5 and 6 of 8 (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Helps Denver.

Phoenix forces turnovers at the 6th-highest rate, and Denver takes threes at one of the lowest rates in the league (28th share) (Predictem, Nov 16 2026). The low three-point rate reduces Denver's blowout variance. Helps Phoenix modestly.
Jamal Murray averages 25.9 points on a career-best 49.4% from three and scored 39 against Phoenix on Oct 30/31, when Denver won 127-120 (a 7-point margin) (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Mixed.
The previews split: Covers takes Nuggets -9.5, Predictem takes Suns +10.5 (Covers; Predictem, Nov 16 2026). Neutral and priced.
games.reasoning: I project Denver by about 9: the ratings say around 7 and the back-to-back at altitude adds a couple. That's against a -10.5 slate and -9.5 close, a 1.5-point gap from the slate and under a point from the close, so it's a pass. Phoenix's rebounding weakness against Jokic is the strongest case for Denver; Denver's modest +1.9 net rating is the case for Phoenix. A late scratch of Booker or Jokic would have decided it.
